title: Guard Active
statement: Implement `solve(user)`. `user` is either the string `none` or a dict with an integer `active` field that is 0 or 1. Return 1 only when the user is a dict and `active` is 1. Return 0 when the user is missing or inactive. Do not index a missing user.
constraints: A missing user is the string none
active is 0 or 1 when the dict is present
hints: Return 0 immediately when user is the string none.
Only an active value of 1 returns 1.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: The expression user and user["active"] is the guard, written without a crash: you never subscript the missing token.

editorial: The expression user and user["active"] is the guard, written without a crash: you never subscript the missing token. An inactive user is present and still not allowed through. Both failures return 0 so the caller has one check.
